title: A tree made from nested llists
hint: Choose Tree and watch the nested llists become branches. Empty llists are empty subtrees, not leaves.
source:
tree = llist(1, llist(2, 3), llist(llist(4), None), 5)
print_llist(tree)

title: A binary tree: entry, left, right
hint: Each node is llist(entry, left, right). The left and right empty branches stay visible.

title: A closure that remembers
hint: Watch balance in E1. Each call changes the same captured binding. Try making a second counter: does it share E1?
source:
def make_counter(balance):
    def add(amount):
        nonlocal balance
        balance = balance + amount
        return balance
    return add

counter = make_counter(10)
print(counter(5))
print(counter(2))

title: Which x does it use?
hint: The enclosing environment comes from where f was defined. Change the x passed to g and predict f's answer.
source:
x = 10

def f(y):
    return x + y

def g(x):
    answer = f(3)
    return answer

print(g(100))

title: Recursion builds frames
hint: Each call gets its own n. Why do all the enclosing-environment buttons point to global env? Try factorial(4).

title: Two independent closures
hint: The two lambda objects remember different calls of make_adder, even though they came from the same line of code.
source:
def make_adder(x):
    return lambda y: x + y

add_two = make_adder(2)
add_ten = make_adder(10)
print(add_two(5))
print(add_ten(5))

title: Shared pairs and mutation
hint: xs and ys point to the same pair. Step past set_head and compare the picture. Try ys = pair(1, None) instead.
source:
xs = pair(1, pair(2, None))
ys = xs
set_head(ys, 99)
print(head(xs))
print(xs is ys)

title: Tail calls pass control on
hint: Compare with ordinary factorial. The previous call does not wait for multiplication: the accumulator carries the answer.

title: Factorial: deferred multiplication
hint: Watch the multiplications build up before they can reduce. Change factorial(3) to factorial(4).

title: Substituting a function argument
hint: A function can be an argument too. Follow how twice replaces f and x before it applies the lambda.

title: Only one branch runs
hint: The predicate reduces first. The branch with division by zero is never evaluated. Try changing 3 > 0 to 3 < 0.
